In [[mathematics]], an '''orthodox semigroup''' is a [[regular semigroup]] whose set of [[idempotent]]s forms a [[subsemigroup]]. In more recent terminology, an orthodox semigroup is a regular [[E-semigroup|''E''-semigroup]].<ref>J. Almeida, [[Jean-Éric Pin|J.-É. Pin]] and P. Weil [http://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/docs/00/06/02/12/PDF/Cambridge.pdf Semigroups whose idempotents form a subsemigroup] updated version of {{Cite journal | doi = 10.1017/S0305004100075332| title = Semigroups whose idempotents form a subsemigroup| journal = [[Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society]]| volume = 111| issue = 2| pages = 241| year = 2008| last1 = Almeida | first1 = J.| last2 = Pin | first2 = J.-É. | last3 = Weil | first3 = P.| s2cid = 6344747| url = https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00019881/document}}</ref> The term ''orthodox semigroup'' was coined by T. E. Hall and presented in a paper published in 1969.<ref>{{cite journal|title=On regular semigroups whose idempotents form a subsemigroup|journal=Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society|date=1969|volume=1|pages=195–208|doi=10.1017/s0004972700041447 | last1 = Hall | first1 = T. E.|issue=2 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=conf>{{cite book|editor1-first=A. H.|editor1-last=Clifford|editor2-first=K. H.|editor2-last=Hofmann|editor3-first=M. W.|editor3-last=Mislove|title=Semigroup Theory and Its Applications: Proceedings of the 1994 Conference Commemorating the Work of [[Alfred H. Clifford]]|date=1996|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9780521576697|page=70}}</ref> Certain special classes of orthodox semigroups had been studied earlier. For example, semigroups that are also unions of groups, in which the sets of idempotents form  subsemigroups were studied by P. H. H. Fantham in 1960.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=P.H.H. Fantham|title=On the Classification of a Certain Type of Semigroup|journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society |date=1960|volume=1|pages=409–427|doi=10.1112/plms/s3-10.1.409}}</ref>

==Examples==
*Consider the [[binary operation]] on the set ''S'' = { ''a'', ''b'', ''c'', ''x'' } defined by the following [[Cayley table]] :
{| class="wikitable" style="margin:1em auto;"
|-
| &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; || &nbsp; ''a'' &nbsp; || &nbsp; ''b'' &nbsp; || &nbsp; ''c'' &nbsp; || &nbsp; ''x'' &nbsp;
|-
| &nbsp; ''a'' || &nbsp; ''a'' || &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''x'' 
|-
| &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''b''
|-
| &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''c''
|-
| &nbsp; ''x'' || &nbsp; ''x'' || &nbsp; ''c'' || &nbsp; ''b'' || &nbsp; ''a''
|} 
:Then ''S'' is an orthodox semigroup under this operation, the subsemigroup of idempotents being { ''a'', ''b'', ''c'' }.<ref name=Howie/>

*[[Inverse semigroup]]s and [[Band (mathematics)|bands]] are examples of orthodox semigroups.<ref name=Grillet>{{cite book|last1=P.A. Grillet|title=Semigroups: An introduction to structure theory|publisher=Marcel Dekker, Inc.|location=New York|page=341}}</ref>

==Some elementary properties==
The set of idempotents in an orthodox semigroup has several interesting properties. Let ''S'' be a regular semigroup and for any ''a'' in ''S'' let ''V''(''a'') denote the set of inverses of ''a''. Then the following are equivalent:<ref name=Howie>{{cite book|last1=J.M. Howie|title=An introduction to semigroup theory|date=1976|publisher=Academic Press|location=London|pages=186–211}}</ref>
*''S'' is orthodox.
*If ''a'' and ''b'' are in ''S'' and if ''x'' is in ''V''(''a'')  and ''y'' is in ''V''(''b'') then ''yx'' is in ''V''(''ab'').
*If ''e'' is an idempotent in ''S'' then every inverse of ''e'' is also an idempotent.
*For every ''a'', ''b'' in ''S'', if ''V''(''a'')&nbsp;∩&nbsp;''V''(''b'') ≠ ∅ then ''V''(''a'') = ''V''(''b'').

==Structure==
The structure of orthodox semigroups have been determined in terms of bands and inverse semigroups. The Hall–Yamada pullback theorem describes this construction. The construction requires the concepts of  [[pullback]]s (in the [[Category theory|category]] of semigroups) and [[K. S. S. Nambooripad|Nambooripad]] representation of a fundamental regular semigroup.<ref name=Grillet/>
